records.context: The window is frameless and the menu bar is what you drag it by. Its first backing store is filled with the splash colour so the compositor cannot expose stale desktop pixels before anything has drawn -- deliberately without ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent``, which is a promise to paint every pixel that this window cannot keep once the application stylesheet clears ``autoFillBackground`` again. Claiming it left whatever was already on application view underneath, and transparent children drew on top: overlapping text in the corner, and flicker on every text surface over the animated backdrop.

Claiming it left whatever was already on screen underneath, and transparent children drew on top: overlapping text in the corner, and flicker on every text surface over the animated backdrop.

records.context: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every independent execution path in this application executes Python. A cancelled independent execution path that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.

records.source: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every thread in this application runs Python. A cancelled thread that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.
records.translation: ``QThread.terminate()``는 내부적으로 ``pthread_cancel``이며, 이 애플리케이션의 모든 스레드는 Python을 실행합니다. 우연히 GIL을 쥐고 있던 스레드가 취소되면 GIL을 결코 해제하지 않아 프로세스 전체가 진행을 멈춥니다. Qt나 PySide 내부에서 취소된 스레드는 힙을 손상시키고, 프로세스는 나중에 무관한 곳에서 죽습니다. 어느 실패도 원인이 된 줄을 알려 주지 않으며, 그래서 :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all`은 "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``"라고 문서화하고 있습니다. 이 함수는 호출자가 그렇게 하는 방법입니다.

records.context: The two differ in exactly one place, and it matters only there. A block registered with :func:`register_widget_qss` is handed the ``opacity`` :func:`stylesheet` was called with, and that is ``None`` when the caller asked for the theme's *designed* scrim rather than any user's setting — the documented meaning of ``surface_opacity=None``, and what every built-in rule in this file honours through :func:`panel_alpha`.

records.translation: 두 함수는 정확히 한 곳에서만 다르며, 그 차이는 그곳에서만 중요합니다. :func:`register_widget_qss`로 등록된 블록은 ``opacity``를 전달받는데, 이는 :func:`stylesheet`가 호출될 때의 값이며, 호출자가 사용자 설정이 아니라 테마의 *설계된* 스크림을 요청한 경우 ``None``입니다. 이것이 ``surface_opacity=None``의 문서화된 의미이며, 이 파일의 모든 기본 제공 규칙이 :func:`panel_alpha`를 통해 따르는 방식입니다.

records.context: :func:`pane_surface` cannot honour it. Its ``None`` means "nobody told me, go and look", so it reads the live page-opacity preference. That is right for the inline and paint-time callers it was written for — Home's aside panels have no ``stylesheet`` argument to plumb through — and wrong inside a block, where ``None`` was already an answer. The consequence was that ``stylesheet("dark")`` emitted ``rgba(22, 23, 25, 0.600)`` for every block that passed it through: a function of its arguments quietly depending on a QSettings value, which made the assertion that the opaque themes emit plain hex pass or fail on module import order.

records.context: Most spaCR application views are plain ``QWidget`` trees. A ``QWidget`` with no QSS rule of its own inherits the blanket ``QWidget {{ background-color: bg }}`` and paints the WINDOW colour — which is not a surface, so no value of the page-opacity preference can reach it. records.context: The sheet in force is not `app.styleSheet()` any more. Per-window sheeting takes the application sheet DOWN on purpose and gives each window its own, so `app.styleSheet()` is empty in every production run -- and this function read that as "nobody opted in" and returned before doing anything. Measured: opening one module registers four blocks (`SettingsBox`, `ClassEditor`, `SettingAlphabetChip`, `TableChip`) and NONE of the four reached the screen that had just imported them. That is the exact defect this function was written for, reintroduced by the change that made the window the sheet's owner.

Measured: opening one module registers four blocks (`SettingsBox`, `ClassEditor`, `SettingAlphabetChip`, `TableChip`) and NONE of the four reached the screen that had just imported them. records.translation: 적용 중인 스타일시트는 더 이상 `app.styleSheet()`가 아닙니다. 창별 스타일시트 방식은 의도적으로 애플리케이션 스타일시트를 내리고 각 창에 자체 스타일시트를 부여하므로, 운영 환경의 모든 실행에서 `app.styleSheet()`는 비어 있습니다. 이 함수는 이를 "nobody opted in"(아무도 선택하지 않음)으로 해석하여 아무것도 하기 전에 반환했습니다. 측정 결과: 모듈 하나를 열면 네 개의 블록(`SettingsBox`, `ClassEditor`, `SettingAlphabetChip`, `TableChip`)이 등록되는데, 네 개 중 어느 것도(NONE) 방금 이들을 가져온 화면에 적용되지 않았습니다. 이는 이 함수가 해결하려고 작성된 바로 그 결함이며, 창을 스타일시트의 소유자로 만든 변경으로 인해 다시 발생했습니다.

records.context: Tag the layout containers with this and the backdrop reaches the eye; leave the cards, panels and inputs alone and they stay the readable surface on top of it. A widget no stylesheet reaches yet, or one in a window whose sheet is held (:func:`_one_sheet_for`), is only tagged: nothing reads the tag until a sheet arrives, and putting a sheet on polishes every widget it reaches. records.context: The sweep cannot be narrowed to exact types. records.context: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. Measured both ways rather than reasoned about.

records.source: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. records.translation: 그 과정에서 Qt 규칙 하나를 감수해야 합니다. ``QWidget``의 **하위 클래스**는 ``WA_StyledBackground``가 설정되지 않으면 QSS 배경을 완전히 무시합니다. 그래서 스타일시트에 일치하는 규칙이 있었는데도 Power의 주의 사항 패널에서는 배경이 그대로 측정되었습니다. 이런 위젯에는 여기서 속성을 설정하지만, ``QAbstractScrollArea``에는 의도적으로 설정하지 않습니다(NOT). 뷰는 이미 뷰포트를 통해 배경을 그리며, 그 위에 스타일이 지정된 채우기를 하나 더 얹으면 다시 두 표면이 겹치는 결함이 생깁니다. 추론이 아니라 두 방식 모두 측정하여 확인했습니다.

records.context: **Space** can be the procedurally generated sky, whose exposure is anchored on the 40th percentile *precisely so a sun stays white-hot* (:data:`spacr.qt.space.TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE`). Only a strong scrim saves text over that, so Space is judged against white and its panels stay much more opaque than Cell's.

Each attached database resolves its own exported-PNG or ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source so multi-plate montages can combine experiments with different storage layouts. The crop mask plane and channels come from :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` or, by default, the run's ``measurements.db`` metadata.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage`는 객체를 선택하고 선택 사유를 기록하며, 이 모듈은 그 이미지 크롭을 찾아 실행의 그림 옆에 표시합니다. 연결된 각 데이터베이스는 자체 내보낸 PNG 또는 ``merged/<fov>.npy`` 소스를 찾으므로, 여러 플레이트 몽타주에서 저장 레이아웃이 다른 실험을 결합할 수 있습니다. 크롭 마스크 평면과 채널은 :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec`에서 오거나, 기본적으로 실행의 ``measurements.db`` 메타데이터에서 옵니다.

records.source: Three properties this file is built around:
records.translation: 이 파일이 기반으로 하는 세 가지 속성:

records.context: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
records.translation: **읽기 전용.** 선택기를 열면 열 이름만 읽고 그 밖에는 아무것도 읽지 않습니다. 연결은 ``file:…?mode=ro``와 ``PRAGMA query_only = ON``을 함께 사용하며, 이는 :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser`와 :mod:`spacr.agreement`가 사용하는 것과 같은 조합이므로 SQLite 자체가 쓰기를 거부합니다. 대화 상자는 결코 열을 만들지 않습니다. *이름*을 반환할 뿐이며, 생성을 담당하는 쓰기 경로(``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, ``ALTER TABLE``로 필요할 때 생성)는 그대로 유지됩니다.

records.context: **Cheap on open.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` is free; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` over a 400 k-row measurement table is not. Opening the dialog runs no count at all. The per-table row figure comes from ``max(_rowid_)`` and is labelled an estimate; a per-column non-null count happens only when the user asks for it by name. (``_rowid_``, not ``rowid`` — see :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, where the difference was a full table scan followed by a ``ValueError``.)
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Cheap on open.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` is free; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` over a 400 k-row measurement table is not. Opening the dialog runs no count at all. The per-table row figure comes from ``max(_rowid_)`` and is labelled an estimate; a per-column non-null count happens only when the user asks for it by name. (``_rowid_``, not ``rowid`` — see :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, where the difference was a full table scan followed by a ``ValueError``.)
records.translation: **열 때 비용이 적음.** ``PRAGMA table_info``는 비용이 거의 없지만, 400 k행 측정 표에 대한 ``SELECT COUNT(*)``는 그렇지 않습니다. 대화 상자를 열 때는 개수 계산을 전혀 하지 않습니다. 표별 행 수는 ``max(_rowid_)``에서 가져오며 추정값으로 표시됩니다. 열별 null이 아닌 값의 개수는 사용자가 이름을 지정해 요청할 때만 계산됩니다. (``_rowid_``를 사용하며 ``rowid``는 사용하지 않습니다. :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`를 참조하십시오. 그 차이로 인해 전체 표 스캔 후 ``ValueError``가 발생했습니다.)

records.context: **Background loading.** The picker does not freeze the GUI. It performs four sequential sqlite queries: open, list tables, read one table's columns, and estimate its rows. Previously, before a dialog appeared, all four queries ran in ``__init__``. Cold measurements were 45 ms for measurements.db, a 383 MB database, and 87 ms for a schema with 1 500 tables. The dialog now selects background mode with ``threaded=True``. All reads are performed by :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. Synchronous mode remains the initial choice; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` explains why.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Cheap is not free, and opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips — open, list tables, read one table's columns, estimate its rows — every one of which used to happen inside ``__init__``, before the modal appeared. Measured cold on a 383 MB measurements.db that is 45 ms, and on a 1 500-table schema 87 ms, entirely between the click and any window. The button now builds the dialog with ``threaded=True`` and the reads arrive from a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The default is still the synchronous mode, deliberately; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` says why.
records.translation: **GUI 스레드 밖에서 실행.** 비용이 적다고 해서 없는 것은 아니며, 선택기를 열려면 sqlite 왕복이 네 번 순차적으로 필요합니다. 열기, 표 나열, 한 표의 열 읽기, 그 표의 행 수 추정이며, 예전에는 이 모든 작업이 모달이 나타나기 전 ``__init__`` 안에서 수행되었습니다. 383 MB measurements.db 파일에서 콜드 상태로 측정하면 45 ms, 1 500개 표 스키마에서는 87 ms였으며, 이 시간이 모두 클릭과 창 표시 사이에 걸렸습니다. 이제 버튼은 ``threaded=True``로 대화 상자를 만들고, 읽기 결과는 :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`에서 도착합니다. 기본값은 의도적으로 여전히 동기 모드이며, 그 이유는 :class:`ColumnPickerDialog`에 설명되어 있습니다.

records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker.SchemaReader.estimate_rows#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.translation: ``_rowid_``로 표기하는 데는 이유가 있습니다. spaCR의 모든 객체 표는 ``rowID``라는 열(플레이트 행, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'``)을 선언하며, SQLite 식별자는 대소문자를 구분하지 않으므로 단순한 ``rowid``는 행 ID가 아니라 *그 열*로 해석됩니다. 측정 데이터베이스에서 ``max(rowid)``는 텍스트 열의 최댓값을 구하기 위해 표 전체를 스캔하며(측정 결과: 200 000행 표에서 웜 21 ms, 콜드 41 ms로, 이 메서드가 피하려는 ``COUNT(*)`` 비용), 이어서 ``int('r16')``이 ``ValueError``를 발생시킵니다. 이 예외는 ``sqlite3.Error``가 아니므로 호출자의 처리기를 벗어나 Qt 이벤트 루프로 빠져나갑니다. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign`, :mod:`spacr.data_manager`도 같은 가림 현상을 처리합니다.

records.context: Control-chart statistics for a screening campaign: limits, rules and Z'.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Control-chart statistics for a screening campaign: limits, rules and Z'.
records.translation: 스크리닝 캠페인을 위한 관리도 통계: 관리 한계, 규칙, Z'.

records.context: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all assume that the positive and negative controls behave the same way on every plate. When the controls drift — the cell line changes, a reagent lot changes, incubation conditions change — every downstream result shifts with them, and the analysis does not detect it, because it normalises to the controls it is given.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all assume that the positive and negative controls behave the same way on every plate. When the controls drift — the cell line changes, a reagent lot changes, incubation conditions change — every downstream result shifts with them, and the analysis does not detect it, because it normalises to the controls it is given.
records.translation: 스크리닝 캠페인은 몇 주에 걸쳐 수행되는 수십 개의 플레이트입니다. 히트 판정, 플레이트 정규화, Z'는 모두 양성 및 음성 대조군이 모든 플레이트에서 같은 방식으로 동작한다고 가정합니다. 대조군이 드리프트하면(세포주가 바뀌거나, 시약 로트가 바뀌거나, 배양 조건이 바뀌면) 모든 하류 결과가 함께 이동하며, 분석은 주어진 대조군에 맞춰 정규화하므로 이를 감지하지 못합니다.

records.context: Sigma **of the plotted statistic** is ``sigma_within / sqrt(n)``, and that is what the zones and the rules are stated in. When subgroup sizes differ between plates the limits differ per plate; they are computed per point rather than averaged, and the result says so.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Sigma **of the plotted statistic** is ``sigma_within / sqrt(n)``, and that is what the zones and the rules are stated in. When subgroup sizes differ between plates the limits differ per plate; they are computed per point rather than averaged, and the result says so.
records.translation: **표시된 통계량의** 시그마는 ``sigma_within / sqrt(n)``이며, 구역과 규칙은 이 값으로 표현됩니다. 플레이트마다 부분군 크기가 다르면 관리 한계도 플레이트마다 다르며, 평균을 내지 않고 점마다 계산하고 결과에 그 사실을 밝힙니다.

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` Explicit, never implicit, and named in the result. spaCR measurements are skewed and one catastrophically bad plate inside the baseline drags the classical centre and MR-bar out far enough to swallow everything after it. The robust variant takes the **median** as the centre and either the median moving range (:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) or the MAD (:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`) as the spread.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` Explicit, never implicit, and named in the result. spaCR measurements are skewed and one catastrophically bad plate inside the baseline drags the classical centre and MR-bar out far enough to swallow everything after it. The robust variant takes the **median** as the centre and either the median moving range (:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) or the MAD (:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`) as the spread.
records.translation: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` 암묵적이지 않고 항상 명시적이며, 결과에 이름이 표시됩니다. spaCR 측정값은 치우쳐 있으며, 기준선 안의 심각하게 나쁜 플레이트 하나가 고전적 중심과 MR-bar를 크게 끌어당겨 그 뒤의 모든 것을 삼켜 버립니다. 로버스트 변형은 **중앙값**을 중심으로 삼고, 퍼짐으로는 중앙 이동 범위(:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) 또는 MAD(:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`)를 사용합니다.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.translation: 두 로버스트 상수는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 *없으며*, 모듈은 이를 따로 유지합니다. 1.4826(:data:`MAD_SCALE`)은 ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``로, 정규 표본의 MAD를 SD의 비편향 추정량으로 만드는 인수입니다. 이동 범위는 ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, 즉 두 관측값의 *차이*의 절댓값이므로 그 척도는 ``sqrt(2)·sigma``이고 중앙값은 ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma``(:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`)입니다. 중앙 이동 범위에 1.4826을 곱하면 시그마를 정확히 ``sqrt(2)``배 과대 추정하여 관리 한계가 41% 넓어지고 드리프트가 가려질 수 있습니다. c4를 감마 함수로 계산하는 것과 같은 이유로, 여기서는 두 상수를 모두 ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)``에서 계산합니다.

records.context: **Limits estimated from an out-of-control baseline are unreliable.** When the baseline itself contains a violation, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` says so. Re-estimating without the flagged plates is *offered* (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) and is off by default, so plates are never removed from the baseline without the user asking. It runs one pass, not iterations to convergence: iterating shrinks the limits onto the tightest subset of the baseline and eventually flags everything.

records.translation: **관리 이탈 상태의 기준선에서 추정한 관리 한계는 신뢰할 수 없습니다.** 기준선 자체에 위반이 있으면 :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats`가 이를 알립니다. 표시된 플레이트를 제외하고 다시 추정하는 기능은 *제공*되지만(:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) 기본적으로 꺼져 있으므로, 사용자가 요청하지 않는 한 플레이트가 기준선에서 제거되지 않습니다. 수렴할 때까지 반복하지 않고 한 번만 실행합니다. 반복하면 관리 한계가 기준선의 가장 좁은 부분 집합으로 줄어들어 결국 모든 것을 표시하게 됩니다.

records.context: This module tracks one control value per plate over run order and puts limits round it, so drift is visible while the application view is running rather than after. records.context: Which points a rule flags is a convention, and an unstated one makes two implementations disagree about the same chart, so it is stated: **every point that is part of the evidence is flagged.** For rule 1 that is the point itself. For the run rules (2, 3, 4, 7, 8) it is every point of the run, reported as one maximal span rather than as a sliding window's worth of overlapping alarms — which is what lets :meth:`ControlChartResult.report` say "laboratory microplates P22–P30 are nine in a row above the centre line" instead of listing three violations. For the "k of m" rules (5, 6) it is the qualifying points only: a window can trigger on two points beyond 2 sigma with a third sitting on the centre line, and that third point is not flagged because it is not part of the evidence.

For the run rules (2, 3, 4, 7, 8) it is every point of the run, reported as one maximal span rather than as a sliding window's worth of overlapping alarms — which is what lets :meth:`ControlChartResult.report` say "plates P22–P30 are nine in a row above the centre line" instead of listing three violations. For the "k of m" rules (5, 6) it is the qualifying points only: a window can trigger on two points beyond 2 sigma with a third sitting on the centre line, and that third point is not flagged because it is not part of the evidence.
records.translation: 규칙이 어떤 점을 표시하는지는 관례이며, 명시되지 않은 관례는 두 구현이 같은 관리도에 대해 서로 다르게 판단하게 만들므로 여기서 명시합니다. **증거의 일부인 모든 점이 표시됩니다.** 규칙 1에서는 그 점 자체입니다. 연속 규칙(2, 3, 4, 7, 8)에서는 연속 구간의 모든 점이며, 슬라이딩 창만큼 겹치는 경보가 아니라 하나의 최대 구간으로 보고됩니다. 그 덕분에 :meth:`ControlChartResult.report`는 위반 세 개를 나열하는 대신 "plates P22–P30 are nine in a row above the centre line"이라고 말할 수 있습니다. "k of m" 규칙(5, 6)에서는 조건을 충족하는 점만 표시됩니다. 창은 2 시그마를 넘는 두 점과 중심선 위에 있는 세 번째 점으로 발동할 수 있으며, 세 번째 점은 증거의 일부가 아니므로 표시되지 않습니다.

records.context: The rule set is selectable, and it has to be, because **running all eight is not eight times the sensitivity**. Each rule has its own in-control false-alarm rate; :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE` carries them, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` does the arithmetic for the set that actually ran, and over a 200-plate campaign it reports the expected number of false alarms. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT` is the Western Electric four (1, 2, 5, 6), which is the set the classical ARL figure was worked out for; :data:`RULES_ALL` is all eight, and :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY` is rule 1 alone for a user who wants limits and nothing else.

records.translation: 규칙 세트는 선택할 수 있으며, 그래야만 합니다. **여덟 개 규칙을 모두 실행한다고 민감도가 여덟 배가 되는 것은 아니기** 때문입니다. 각 규칙에는 관리 상태에서의 고유한 오경보율이 있습니다. :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE`가 이를 담고, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats`가 실제로 실행된 세트에 대해 계산하며, 200개 플레이트 캠페인에서 예상되는 오경보 수를 보고합니다. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT`는 고전적인 ARL 수치가 산출된 세트인 Western Electric 네 규칙(1, 2, 5, 6)이고, :data:`RULES_ALL`은 여덟 개 전부이며, :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY`는 관리 한계 외에는 원하지 않는 사용자를 위한 규칙 1 단독입니다.

records.context: The casing is load-bearing; the orientation is what makes it part of the rain. It used to be stored as a single token in a single cell and drawn horizontally, overflowing rightwards across its neighbours — which read as a label pasted over the effect rather than as part of it, and cost the renderer a whole second paint pass, measured token widths, widened dirty rectangles and a cleared backing rectangle so neighbouring glyphs did not tangle with the letters. None of that machinery exists now: every cell holds exactly one character, so the word is cached and blitted like any other glyph and cannot overdraw anything. See :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` for the rate and what it works out to in practice.

records.context: 1. *The timer stops whenever the widget is not on application view* — hidden, or in a minimised window. Zero frames, zero CPU. 2. *Each string is pre-rendered once into an opaque pixmap* with the background already composited in, and blitted at its current offset every frame. Drawing 5400 glyphs with ``drawText`` costs 35 ms a frame; the same glyphs as 120 opaque strips cost 0.46 ms — and an opaque strip is 25x cheaper to blit than a translucent one, which is why the alpha is baked in rather than applied by the painter. A strip is re-rendered only when its column respawns or the styling changes; the cache is ~7 MB at 1920x1080. :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop` gives that up deliberately — a picture under the rain is not a constant to bake against — so the translucent path is taken only by the themes that have a wallpaper to show, and dark and light keep the numbers above. 3. *Only the columns that moved are repainted.* Positions are quantised to whole cells, so a column is dirty only when its integer row changes — slow columns cost nothing on most ticks. See :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS` for where partial repaints stop paying.

records.source: 1. *The timer stops whenever the widget is not on screen* — hidden, or in a minimised window. Zero frames, zero CPU. 2. *Each string is pre-rendered once into an opaque pixmap* with the background already composited in, and blitted at its current offset every frame. Drawing 5400 glyphs with ``drawText`` costs 35 ms a frame; the same glyphs as 120 opaque strips cost 0.46 ms — and an opaque strip is 25x cheaper to blit than a translucent one, which is why the alpha is baked in rather than applied by the painter. A strip is re-rendered only when its column respawns or the styling changes; the cache is ~7 MB at 1920x1080. :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop` gives that up deliberately — a picture under the rain is not a constant to bake against — so the translucent path is taken only by the themes that have a wallpaper to show, and dark and light keep the numbers above. 3. *Only the columns that moved are repainted.* Positions are quantised to whole cells, so a column is dirty only when its integer row changes — slow columns cost nothing on most ticks. See :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS` for where partial repaints stop paying.
records.translation: 1. *위젯이 화면에 없을 때마다 타이머가 멈춥니다* — 숨겨졌거나 최소화된 창에 있을 때입니다. 프레임 0개, CPU 0. 2. *각 문자열은 배경이 이미 합성된 불투명 픽스맵으로 한 번 미리 렌더링되며*, 매 프레임 현재 오프셋에 블릿됩니다. ``drawText``로 글리프 5400개를 그리면 프레임당 35 ms가 들지만, 같은 글리프를 불투명 스트립 120개로 그리면 0.46 ms가 듭니다. 또한 불투명 스트립은 반투명 스트립보다 블릿 비용이 25x 저렴하므로, 알파를 그리기 도구가 적용하지 않고 미리 구워 넣습니다. 스트립은 해당 열이 다시 생성되거나 스타일이 바뀔 때만 다시 렌더링되며, 캐시는 1920x1080에서 약 ~7 MB입니다. :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop`은 의도적으로 이를 포기합니다. 비 아래의 그림은 미리 구워 넣을 수 있는 상수가 아니기 때문입니다. 따라서 반투명 경로는 보여 줄 배경 화면이 있는 테마에서만 사용되며, 다크와 라이트 테마는 위의 수치를 유지합니다. 3. *움직인 열만 다시 그립니다.* 위치는 셀 단위로 양자화되므로 열의 정수 행이 바뀔 때만 더티 상태가 되며, 느린 열은 대부분의 틱에서 비용이 들지 않습니다. 부분 다시 그리기가 더 이상 이득이 되지 않는 지점은 :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS`를 참조하십시오.

records.context: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one application view that has a rain.

records.source: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one screen that has a rain.
records.translation: 비는 구조상 불투명한 배경입니다. 변경된 셀만 다시 그리므로 그 셀을 *지울* 수 있어야 하며, 반투명 색상으로 지우면 이전 프레임이 번집니다. 다크와 라이트 테마에서는 뒤에 있는 것이 비가 정확히 재현할 수 있는 평면 ``bg``이므로 이것이 올바른 절충입니다. 이미지 테마에서는 그렇지 않습니다. 평면 색상은 배경 화면과 전혀 다르며, 비가 있는 유일한 화면에서 불투명한 비가 사진을 완전히 가렸습니다.

records.source: Deliberately does NOT consult `population()`. Hit-testing a gate is pure geometry -- is this coordinate inside this shape -- and needs no rows at all. Asking for the population first meant that whenever it was unavailable, dragging died silently: `population()` returns None when the active gate no longer exists, which is exactly the state left behind by DELETING a gate. The remaining gate then looked "fixed and I cannot move".
records.translation: 의도적으로 `population()`을 참조하지 않습니다(NOT). 게이트 적중 검사는 순수한 기하 문제(이 좌표가 이 도형 안에 있는가)이며 행이 전혀 필요하지 않습니다. 모집단을 먼저 요청하면 모집단을 사용할 수 없을 때마다 끌기가 조용히 멈췄습니다. 활성 게이트가 더 이상 존재하지 않으면 `population()`은 None을 반환하는데, 이는 정확히 게이트를 DELETING(삭제)한 뒤 남는 상태입니다. 그러면 남은 게이트가 "fixed and I cannot move"(고정되어 움직일 수 없음)처럼 보였습니다.

records.context: The offered remedy is a **log10 transform**, :data:`TRANSFORM_LOG10`, which turns a lognormal into a Gaussian and makes the fence mean what it appears to mean. It is **never implicit**: a transform silently applied would change what ``outlier_score`` is in units of without the user asking. And it **refuses** rather than fudges on non-positive values — ``log10`` of a zero ``pathogen_area`` is ``-inf``, and an implicit ``+1`` or a dropped row would be an invented measurement or a self-selected population. The refusal names the feature and the count.

And it **refuses** rather than fudges on non-positive values — ``log10`` of a zero ``pathogen_area`` is ``-inf``, and an implicit ``+1`` or a dropped row would be an invented measurement or a self-selected population. records.translation: 제공되는 해결책은 **log10 변환**인 :data:`TRANSFORM_LOG10`이며, 로그 정규 분포를 Gaussian으로 바꾸어 울타리가 보이는 그대로의 의미를 갖게 합니다. 이 변환은 **결코 암묵적이지 않습니다**. 조용히 적용된 변환은 사용자가 요청하지도 않았는데 ``outlier_score``의 단위를 바꾸게 됩니다. 또한 양수가 아닌 값에서는 얼버무리지 않고 **거부합니다**. ``log10``을 0인 ``pathogen_area``에 적용하면 ``-inf``이며, 암묵적인 ``+1``이나 행 제외는 지어낸 측정값이나 스스로 선택된 모집단이 됩니다. 거부 메시지는 특성과 개수를 밝힙니다.

records.context: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.translation: **isolation forest가 아니라 MCD를 쓰는 이유.** 둘 다 "multivariate outlier detectors"(다변량 이상치 검출기)이지만 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 없습니다.

records.context: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#21
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.
records.translation: **MCD는 아핀 등변성을 가집니다.** ``area``를 px^2에서 um^2로 재조정하거나 특성의 임의의 선형 결합으로 회전해도, 적합된 중심과 공분산이 함께 변환되므로 모든 거리와 모든 표시가 변하지 않습니다. 이는 :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model`이 PCA 전에 표준화하는 근거로 드는 것과 같은 불변성 논증이며, 여기서 척도 조정 옵션이 필요 없는 이유입니다. 척도가 곧 공분산*입니다*. 트리 앙상블은 원시 좌표로 분할하므로 등변성이 없으며, 그 답은 단위에 따라 달라집니다.

records.context: Multiple testing is not optional here. Flagging N objects at level alpha is N hypothesis tests; :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats` states both the expected count of false flags at the chosen alpha and the Bonferroni-corrected alpha (``alpha / N``) that would hold the *family-wise* rate at the nominal level, so the user can pick which of the two questions they are asking.

Flagging N objects at level alpha is N hypothesis tests; :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats` states both the expected count of false flags at the chosen alpha and the Bonferroni-corrected alpha (``alpha / N``) that would hold the *family-wise* rate at the nominal level, so the user can pick which of the two questions they are asking.
records.translation: 여기서 다중 검정은 선택 사항이 아닙니다. 유의 수준 alpha에서 N개 객체를 표시하는 것은 N개의 가설 검정입니다. :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`는 선택한 alpha에서 예상되는 거짓 표시 수와, *가족별* 오류율을 명목 수준으로 유지하는 Bonferroni 보정 alpha(``alpha / N``)를 모두 밝히므로, 사용자는 두 질문 중 어느 것을 묻고 있는지 고를 수 있습니다.

records.context: Take 60 objects per well, a feature whose within-well spread is sigma, and a well whose whole population is shifted by 0.9 sigma. The **object** rule at k = 3.5 asks each object to exceed 3.5 sigma; a 0.9 sigma shift moves that requirement to 2.6 sigma, which about one object in 200 clears — so the bad well contributes a fraction of one extra flagged object and disappears into the ordinary tail. The **well** rule compares well *medians*, whose sampling spread is only ``1.2533 * sigma / sqrt(60) = 0.16 sigma``; the same shift is then 5.6 robust SDs and the well is unmistakable. The two tests have wildly different power against the same defect, which is why both are run and both are reported.

records.context: The alternative considered and not taken is the Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), which is the statistically better answer: it has a 50% breakdown point, needs no symmetry assumption, and does not collapse on tied data. It is not used because the naive form is O(n^2) — unusable on the 10^5–10^6 object rows spaCR routinely produces — and the O(n log n) algorithm is a page of intricate code to maintain for a path that is only ever reached when the MAD has *already* collapsed. The mean absolute deviation has a 0% breakdown point and that is stated plainly rather than glossed: it is a stopgap that keeps a degenerate column from flagging its whole tail, not a robust estimator. If the fallback fires, the column is probably not continuous enough for this test.

records.context: Filtering changes a Q-Q plot in a way it does not change a volcano. A volcano of the guides is the same dots with some removed; a Q-Q of the guides is a different diagnostic -- the expected quantiles are recomputed over 900 tests instead of 1,200, so the diagonal moves, the inflation figure at the median is a different number, and the excess in the histogram's first bin is this family's excess and not the run's. A reader who does not know which one is on application view cannot use either.

records.source: Filtering changes a Q-Q plot in a way it does not change a volcano. A volcano of the guides is the same dots with some removed; a Q-Q of the guides is a different diagnostic -- the expected quantiles are recomputed over 900 tests instead of 1,200, so the diagonal moves, the inflation figure at the median is a different number, and the excess in the histogram's first bin is this family's excess and not the run's. A reader who does not know which one is on screen cannot use either.
records.translation: 필터링은 화산 플롯과 달리 Q-Q 플롯을 바꿉니다. 가이드 RNA의 화산 플롯은 같은 점에서 일부를 뺀 것이지만, 가이드 RNA의 Q-Q 플롯은 다른 진단입니다. 기대 분위수가 1,200개가 아니라 900개 검정에 대해 다시 계산되므로 대각선이 움직이고, 중앙값에서의 팽창 수치가 다른 숫자가 되며, 히스토그램 첫 구간의 초과분은 실행 전체가 아니라 이 계열의 초과분입니다. 화면에 어느 쪽이 표시되었는지 모르는 독자는 둘 다 사용할 수 없습니다.

records.source: A permutation run's table is the union of two schemas: a guide row has ``guide`` and ``wells_with_guide``, a gene row has ``gene``, ``wells_with_gene`` and ``guides_in_gene``. Showing the union means that whichever level is chosen, a third of the columns are empty -- and the gene the reader is looking for is named thirteen columns to the right of a blank ``guide`` cell.
records.translation: 순열 실행의 표는 두 스키마의 합집합입니다. 가이드 RNA 행에는 ``guide``와 ``wells_with_guide``가 있고, 유전자 행에는 ``gene``, ``wells_with_gene``, ``guides_in_gene``가 있습니다. 합집합을 보여 주면 어느 수준을 선택하든 열의 3분의 1이 비어 있으며, 독자가 찾는 유전자는 빈 ``guide`` 셀에서 오른쪽으로 열세 열 떨어진 곳에 표시됩니다.

records.context: Dropping a column that no visible row fills is safe because it carries no value for this selection: "how many microplate sample positions hold this guide" has no answer for a gene. The identity and significance columns in :data:`TABLE_KEEP_COLUMNS` stay regardless.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.regression_results.for_table#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Dropping a column that no visible row fills is safe because it carries no value for this selection: "how many wells hold this guide" has no answer for a gene. The identity and significance columns in :data:`TABLE_KEEP_COLUMNS` stay regardless.
records.translation: 보이는 행 중 어느 것도 채우지 않는 열은 이 선택에 대해 값을 담고 있지 않으므로 빼도 안전합니다. "how many wells hold this guide"(이 가이드 RNA를 가진 웰 수)는 유전자에 대해 답이 없습니다. :data:`TABLE_KEEP_COLUMNS`의 식별 및 유의성 열은 항상 유지됩니다.

records.source: ``results.csv`` is meant to hold every level a run produced -- a fitted run at ``level='both'`` writes its guide and gene rows into one table and the panel filters them apart by the ``level`` column.
records.translation: ``results.csv``는 실행이 만든 모든 수준을 담도록 되어 있습니다. ``level='both'``로 적합한 실행은 가이드 RNA 행과 유전자 행을 하나의 표에 기록하며, 패널은 ``level`` 열로 이를 걸러 나눕니다.

records.context: Older permutation runs did not: they tested genes, corrected them as their own family, wrote them to ``results_gene.csv``, and left ``results.csv`` holding guides alone. The writer now follows the rule, and this function also reads those older runs.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.regression_results.read_run_tables#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Older permutation runs did not: they tested genes, corrected them as their own family, wrote them to ``results_gene.csv``, and left ``results.csv`` holding guides alone. The writer now follows the rule, and this function also reads those older runs.
records.translation: 이전 순열 실행은 그렇지 않았습니다. 유전자를 검정하고 자체 계열로 보정한 뒤 ``results_gene.csv``에 기록했으며, ``results.csv``에는 가이드 RNA만 남겼습니다. 이제 기록기는 규칙을 따르며, 이 함수는 그런 이전 실행도 읽습니다.

records.translation: 형제 파일은 기본 표에 아직 없는 수준을 가져올 때만 병합되므로, 이미 둘 다 담은 실행은 건드리지 않으며 어떤 것도 두 번 집계되지 않습니다.

records.context: model : object or None Fitted model.
